question.problem: Which of the following expressions gives all of the zeros of the function $f(x)=2\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{4})?$ Assume that $n$ is an integer.
question.worked_solution:
The zeros of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡x$ are given by 

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

To find the zeros of $f(x)=2\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{4}),$ we replace the $x$ on the left-hand side of the above with $(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{4}).$ This gives

$$
\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{4}=\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi .
$$

Solving for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\pi }{4} & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi  \\ \frac{x}{2} & =\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi -\frac{\pi }{4} \\ \frac{x}{2} & =\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{2}+2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the zeros are $x=\frac{\pi }{2}+2n\pi ,$ where $n$ is an integer.
